1. Core Clinical Tension: An 18-year-old male presents with vague chest discomfort, normal physical examination, normal chest radiograph, but focal apico-infero-posterior ischemic changes on ECG and a large, well-defined intramyocardial fluid-filled cyst on echocardiography. The tension lies in differentiating an unusual parasitic cyst from primary cardiac neoplasms, pericardial cysts, or structural ventricular pseudoaneurysms in an otherwise healthy adolescent.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The admission breakpoint occurs immediately following initial emergency evaluation, ECG, chest radiography, and preliminary transthoracic echocardiography identifying the intramyocardial fluid-filled cyst, prior to advanced CT imaging revealing hepatic cysts and surgical intervention.
3. Differential Distinctions: Cardiac myxoma/fibroma (typically solid, intraluminal, or pedunculated, unlike this fluid-filled intramyocardial mass), pericardial cyst (typically extracardiac and nestled in the right cardiophrenic angle), and ventricular pseudoaneurysm (typically follows myocardial infarction or trauma with turbulent flow). Confirmatory thoracic/abdominal CT demonstrating coexisting multivesicular hepatic cyst and intraoperative cystectomy establish echinococcosis.
case_prompt: An 18-year-old male is referred to the clinic presenting with chest discomfort. Physical examination is entirely normal. Chest radiography reveals normal cardiothoracic contours and clear lung fields. A 12-lead electrocardiogram demonstrates sinus rhythm with ischemic changes localized to the apico-infero-posterior myocardium. Initial two-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography reveals a single, large, well-defined oval fluid-filled intramyocardial cyst measuring 39 x 56 x 38 mm in the infero-postero-apical segment, which protrudes slightly into the pericardium but predominantly bulges into the left ventricular cavity.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Cardiac myxoma or primary intracardiac tumor
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Primary intracardiac tumors like myxomas are generally intraluminal, pedunculated, or solid masses rather than a well-circumscribed, pure fluid-filled intramyocardial cyst.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Two-dimensional-TTE (2DTTE) (Supplementary data online, Movie S1) showed a single, large oval cyst (39 x 56 x 38 mm). The edge was well defined (Panel A), it was intramyocardial and fluid-filled.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Left ventricular pseudoaneurysm or true aneurysm
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Pseudoaneurysms result from myocardial rupture contained by pericardium following infarction or trauma with a visible neck and turbulent flow, whereas this was an ellipsoid, well-defined intramyocardial fluid collection in an otherwise healthy young patient.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: showing an apico-infero-posterior intramyocardial ellipsoid cystic mass with liquid content and well-defined edges.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Pericardial cysts are benign congenital cysts typically situated extracardiac in the cardiophrenic angles (most commonly right), whereas this cyst was predominantly intramyocardial and projected into the left ventricular lumen.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: it was intramyocardial and fluid-filled. It was located in the infero-postero-apical segment, protruding into the pericardium but mainly bulging into the left ventricular cavity

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Chest computed tomography demonstrating a concurrent multivesicular hepatic cyst alongside the intramyocardial cyst, followed by surgical resection and aspiration of cystic material from the left ventricular myocardium, establishing hydatid disease.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Chest computed tomography (CT) (Panel C) confirmed the presence of a left ventricular intramyocardial cyst and also a multivesicular hepatic cyst.

editor_comments: Distilled strictly adhering to the admission breakpoint before advanced thoracoabdominal CT and surgery. Zero leakage of Echinococcus, hydatid, or hepatic cysts in the prompt. Quotes verified against source text.
